newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Spring/White Wheat - Bids fall, sales slow.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Spring/White Wheat - Bids fall, sales slow.

text.p: Basis bids for dark northern spring wheat retraced downward on Thursday, shadowing moves in MGE futures, several cash grain dealers said.

Farmer sales remained slow as producers held on to supplies in hopes of higher prices. Dealers also noted that new crop conditions were uncertain after a long dry spell and some farmers were worried about committing to new crop sales without knowing how well the crops would yield.
Bids for 13 percent protein hard red winter wheat remained high as dealers continued to scout for higher proteins. The dry weather stressed crops and may have lowered proteins.

One Montana dealer said he did not expect farmers to sell much of the lower protein crops as prices deteriorated. He said producers would likely opt to put the grain under USDA loan instead in hopes of better prices.
"They haven't released our (USDA) loan rates yet but they'll probably be around $2.60 a bushel," he said.
"We're bidding around $2.80 for ordinary (low) protein," he added. "They'll probably put it under a nine-month loan program and see what happens."
